title: Implement precommit-credit rollback protocol for speculative streaming allocs
creator: Priya Shah
description: Background: We currently pre-allocate "credits" in the metering pipeline when a streaming session begins speculative decoding or when a client requests a large prefix pre-warm. In high-throughput tail scenarios and during client aborts/reconnects, those precommitted credits are sometimes not reconciled correctly and either bleed into final charges or are orphaned in the ledger. This ticket implements a formal precommit-credit lifecycle with an explicit rollback protocol and audit hooks to ensure final charges equal consumed tokens across HTTP and WS streaming flows.
background: Symptoms observed: 1) Customers report occasional small overcharges after aborted streams during reconnect storms. 2) Internal audits show transient 'PRECOMMIT' ledger entries never transitioned to COMMITTED or ABORTED for up to 24h in rare failure modes. 3) Existing heuristics (time-based expiry) are not deterministic and complicate post-facto corrections. Related investigation: ENG-314159 (clock-skew dedup) found a few repository traces where precommit timestamps were mis-ordered leading to missed finalization.
proposed_solution: Introduce three-state precommit ledger items (PRECOMMIT, COMMITTED, ABORTED) with idempotent transitions and a compensating rollback protocol. Key pieces: 1) On stream start, create PRECOMMIT entry with session_id, precommit_id, estimated_credit. 2) Runtime emits explicit COMMIT when final token count for that session is known; if session ends without COMMIT (client abort, reconnect delegate) we emit ABORT with observed consumed tokens (likely 0). 3) A reconciliation worker periodically scans PRECOMMIT entries older than N seconds and attempts finalization via a deterministic heuristic and last-seen-session-state; if unable, it creates a compensating ABORT and flags for human audit. 4) All transitions are written with monotonic sequence numbers to ledger to avoid duplicate application. 5) Add non-breaking API/contract to frontends so that they can ack COMMIT/ABORT; fall back to server-side finalization if ack missing. 6) Emit structured audit events linking precommit_id -> final_ledger_id for traceability.
acceptance_criteria: New precommit entries are created on speculative streaming starts with required fields (precommit_id, session_id, estimated_credit)
COMMIT and ABORT transitions are idempotent and resilient to at-least-once event delivery
Reconciliation worker finalizes >99.99% of PRECOMMIT items within 60s in staging load tests
No customer-facing charge increases in canary traffic; charges equal final consumed tokens for 1000 randomized simulated aborts
Structured audit link available in Console for each final charge referencing originating precommit_id
tasks: Design ledger schema diff and add precommit state (ENG DB migration)
Implement precommit create path in streaming ingress middleware
Emit COMMIT/ABORT messages from runtime and make transitions idempotent
Build reconciliation worker with backoff and deterministic heuristics
Add audit event producer and Console link for tracing precommit -> final
E2E tests: simulate aborts, reconnects, and high tail latencies
Load test in staging and run billing delta analysis vs control group
Docs: update API contract for streaming ack semantics and developer guide
notes: Tradeoffs: Short expiry reduces orphaned precommits but increases false aborts when clients are slow; we chose 60s as a conservative starting point for staging.
We considered immediate finalization on stream close but cannot rely on client close semantics for long-lived mobile networks.
Monotonic sequence numbers are required to avoid replay double-applications from the events bus (Kafka at-least-once delivery).
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Shah: Triage notes - Priority raised after customer report and a small but reproducible leakage seen in billing audit. Assigning to Diego for design + prototype.

2026-03-11 Diego Martinez: Spike complete. Implemented a prototype reconciliation worker and validated idempotent transition logic in a unit harness. Observed race when stream COMMIT and reconciliation both run concurrently; resolved with sequence numbers and compare-and-set on ledger state.

2026-03-12 Ava Kumar (SRE): Can we ensure reconciliation worker's backoff doesn't create a window for double-charges? Suggest emitting compensating ABORT and a reconciliation marker event to avoid later COMMITs overwriting. Added to design notes.
2026-03-13 Diego Martinez: Working on DB migration script. Will open a PR for the ledger schema change by EOD. QA plan drafted; need 2 engineers for canary validation next week.
2026-03-13 Priya Shah: Reminder to add Console link to cost breakdowns and to coordinate with billing team for retrospective audit tooling.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag the precommit lifecycle in runtime; default off for legacy traffic
Canary 5% of traffic in us-west-2 for 24h and run billing parity checks
Gradual rollout to 25% -> 50% -> 100% as reconciliations remain healthy
If parity drift detected >0.01% for 1h, pause rollout and open incident
rollback_plan: Flip feature flag off to stop creating new PRECOMMIT entries
Run reconciliation in read-only mode to finalize outstanding PRECOMMITs into compensating ABORTs
If DB migration caused issues, rollback via migration down script and restore snapshot of ledger cluster
Notify customers and billing team if any manual corrections are required
qa_approach: Unit tests for idempotent transitions and CAS semantics
Integration tests simulating at-least-once delivery and reordered events
Staging load test with synthetic mobile clients that randomly abort and reconnect
Billing parity test comparing canary vs control over 24h with randomized seeds
